title: Integral morphisms of algebraic spaces are affine and universally closed
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $f$ is integral: for every scheme $T\to X$, the fibre product $Y\times_XT$ is represented by a scheme integral over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $f$ is affine, meaning that these scheme base changes are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and universally closed: for every algebraic space $X\prime\to X$, the map $|Y\times_XX\prime|\to|X\prime|$ is closed, with the atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. No finite-type, surjectivity, quasi-compactness of $X$, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to X$, the hypothesis gives an integral scheme morphism $Y\times_XT\to T$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] it is affine. This is exactly the scheme-test definition of affineness in the statement, so $f$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0415 (lemma-integral-universally-closed), forward implication, expanded using Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), proof of (3) to (4).

proof.text: Fix any algebraic space $X\prime\to X$ and put $Z=Y\times_XX\prime$, with projection $g:Z\to X\prime$. These fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For any representable etale scheme test $a:T\to X\prime$, put $V=Y\times_XT$. It is a scheme integral over $T$ by the hypothesis. The fibre-product universal property identifies $V$ with $Z\times_{X\prime}T$; write $q:V\to Z$ and $h:V\to T$ for the projections. By [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed], $h$ is universally closed, hence its underlying point map is closed. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], the scheme map $q$ induces a continuous map $|V|\to|Z|$.

source.place: Tag 0415 (lemma-integral-universally-closed), forward implication, expanded using Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), proof of (3) to (4).

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq|Z|$ be closed. We claim $|a|^{-1}(|g|(C))=|h|(|q|^{-1}(C))$. One inclusion follows from $gq=ah$. For the other, choose $t\in|T|$ and $z\in C$ with $a(t)=g(z)$. By [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], representatives of $t$ and $z$ agree in $X\prime$ after a common field extension $M$. Their two maps from $\operatorname{Spec}M$ therefore give a map to $Z\times_{X\prime}T=V$ by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its point class projects to $z$ and $t$, so it belongs to $|q|^{-1}(C)$ and proves the claimed inclusion. This uses equality of point classes, not a cartesian equality of underlying topological spaces.

source.place: Tag 0415 (lemma-integral-universally-closed), forward implication, expanded using Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), proof of (3) to (4).

proof.text: Continuity of $|q|$ makes $|q|^{-1}(C)$ closed, and closedness of $|h|$ makes its image closed in $|T|$. By step 3 this image is $|a|^{-1}(|g|(C))$. This holds for every representable etale scheme test $a:T\to X\prime$. The final-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology], applied to complements, says precisely that $|g|(C)$ is closed in $|X\prime|$. Thus $g$ is closed for every $X\prime\to X$, proving universal closedness without any additional hypothesis.

Step 2: lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers gives the fibre products, so V=Y×_X T≅Z×_{X'}T; pqf-lem-integral-univclosed (01WM, integral implies universally closed) makes h closed; lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover makes |q| continuous, and def-a1-space-point-topology identifies its topology with the atlas topology.
